items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1974-01-01
items.q: I could organize a band like the Don Albert Band from the year of 1929 to say 1932... Even old man Johnson, as old as he was, he considered himself one of us.

ctx.x: Well, if you could organize a band now, get anybody who wanted to, who would play these? Who would you hire a band?

If I could organize a band again, and I could organize a band like the Don Albert Band from the year of 1929 to say 1932, and I could get individuals that was in that band, yes, I would organize a band tomorrow. And I'm not going to find them. I'm not going to find them. You have to face backs. Those were loyal musicians. They treated each other as though they were brothers. Even old man Johnson, as old as he was, he considered himself one of us. Yes, I'd organize a band, but you can't find them. So then you just…
Well, I find that so many musicians want to play the lead, man. That's all I do. They're on that mind. It doesn't matter what instrument they play, they want to be strong.

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1973-12-30
items.q: That's the one that Richard McCawfield and myself and Richard Johnson came.

ctx.x: There was a little band in Dallas where Blaine Johnson was here. That's the one that Richard McCawfield and myself and Richard Johnson came. He was a very, very, very person that got sick and he would stop playing.
Oh, but did he play with you ever?

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1974-01-01
items.q: they didn't want to place them with the family band, the Peripets. And they said, no, they want to be with me.

ctx.x: Well, I was surprised, you know. I told him about the papers of the death makers. I didn't even know he was living in the world. Right.

Well, that was a sort of a shock. Because I didn't, I don't think Richard was sick. He just sat apart from me. That's nice that I'm so excited. You never know. Now, the house where I was born in New Orleans is still there. My brother is still living here. I was born in it. My sister was born in it. My sister was dead.
Now, that's Leo. Now, Leo is the brother that's living here.
